title: TLS certificates, free issuance and automatic renewal

videos.script: A padlock in the address bar. Most people read it as: this site is safe. It says something narrower, and more useful. {{padlock}} It says the connection is encrypted. And it says the server at the other end really holds this name. Nothing about whether the site is honest. {{two-jobs}} The proof is a certificate. Somebody your computer already trusts has signed a statement: this key belongs to this name. {{signed}} For years that signature cost money and a day of paperwork, and certificates expired on servers nobody remembered. {{expired}} Then a free authority, Let's Encrypt, made the whole thing a protocol a program can follow. Prove you control the name, receive a certificate, renew it every few weeks without a person involved. {{acme}} In this lesson you make a certificate that signs itself, and see why nobody should trust it. Then you run a practice certificate authority on your own server, and get a real chain from it with certbot. {{practice}} You configure Nginx to serve it, send all plain traffic to HTTPS, and make renewal happen on its own. And you watch Caddy do every one of those steps by itself. {{caddy}}
